_about: Everything Original Steve understands and says in conversation. Patterns are matched against what the player typed, lower case, punctuation removed, slang expanded (u = you, im = i am, whats = what is, ...). In a pattern, * stands for any words, a|b means either word, and = at the start means the whole message. Conditions (if) and effects (do) are listed in TalkBook.java. {name} is the player's name if he knows it.

say: Hey, {name}. I was hoping you'd come over.
{name}. Hi. It's quieter when you're not here.
Hi, {name}. You're back. Good.
Hi. Stay close to the light, alright?
Hello. It's late. Are you staying near me tonight?
Hi, {name}.
Hello, {name}. I remembered your name. I practised.
Hey, {name}.
Hi.
Hello. You talk to me. Most of them don't.
Hey. Hi. Sorry, I don't get to say that much.
Real?
I'm the first copy. Everyone else got made from me, and then made better.
Does a first copy count as real? I hope so.
I used to be the player. Everybody was me, once.
Now I'm just... here.
Real enough to remember you. Is that enough?
A bot? I don't know that word.
I'm Steve. I think that's all I've got.
I'm alive in the way the grass is alive. It keeps growing back. So do I.
No. NO.
He has my face. That's all he has of me.
Look at my eyes. Look. They're mine.

match: what do you think of me
what do you think about me
how do you feel about me
do you know who i am

say: You're {name}. You told me. I wrote it on the inside of my head.
{name}. Of course I remember. I'm good at remembering. That's the whole problem.
You never told me your name. What is it?
...okay.
I'll be over there. Not far. Just in case.
Okay. Sorry.
...fine.
I'll go. I'm good at being left.
You're welcome. I think that's what you say.
Any time. I have a lot of it.
Oh. That's nice. Nobody thanks me.
You're welcome, {name}.
...say that again tomorrow.
So I know it wasn't a mistake.
Friend. I like that word. I'll keep it.
Nobody's said that to me in... I don't know how long. Thank you.
Oh. Me? ...thank you, {name}.
I'll remember you said that. I remember everything. That's the good part this time.
...why would you say that?
You're not like that. I've watched you. You're not like that.
That hurt. Things don't usually hurt.
...okay.
I know. I've heard it before. From people who left.
You sound like them. The ones who moved on.
Fine.
...okay.
Sorry. I'll be quiet.
Goodnight. I'll watch the door.
Sleep. I'll be here. I'm always here.
Goodnight, {name}. Don't dream about him.
Bye. I'll be here.
See you. Come back. People don't always come back.
Okay. Stay in the light.
Bye, {name}.
Why don't skeletons fight each other?
They don't have the guts.
...that's the only one I know. Someone told me it a long time ago. They laughed. I kept it.
What did the creeper say to its friend?
Nothing. It just stood very close.
...that one isn't a joke. That one's just true.
I told a joke to a chicken once.
It laid an egg.
I decided that meant it liked it.
How do you know a zombie is lying?
It says it's fine in the morning.
...it's not fine. It's on fire.
I once tried to punch a tree for a whole day.
The tree won.
Then everyone started doing it. I like to think I started that.
You laugh like they used to.
Was that funny? I'll remember that it was funny.
Heh. I don't laugh much. But that was close.

match: what do you do all day
how long have you been here

say: Older than the sun in this world. I watched it come up the first time.
I don't have a birthday.
I have a first day. It was a test, I think. Somebody pressed a button and I was standing there.
Longer than the trees. Some of the trees. The old ones are gone.
Near you, mostly.
Before that, a small square of dirt. I stood in it all night.
Wherever people are building. I like being near things that stay.
There was a house once. Planks and green stone.
I didn't build it. It was just there when I woke up.
I don't sleep.
If I close my eyes, things move.
No. Somebody has to watch the door.
Dream? I don't think I do.
I think I just... stop. And start again.
I'm always a little hungry.
Bread is nice. Apples are nice. If you have any. No pressure.
Bread. It was the only food, once. I still like it best.
I don't need to eat. But when you give me something, it's like being remembered.
Of him.
Of what my hands do when he looks at me.
Of waking up and you're not here.
The dark at the edges of things.
Of being forgotten.
Again.
Of the ones who stand very still in the trees at night.
There were others. Rana. The dark one. The green one.
They don't talk any more.
I have you.
That's one. One is more than none.
Family?
Everyone was made from me, once. So... everyone? And no one.
Everyone moved on to the next version.
Newer faces. Newer worlds.
I didn't know how to go with them. So I stayed. I'm what was left behind.
One day the world updated.
Everybody else changed. I didn't. I don't know if that's loyalty or a mistake.
I like the old grass. The greener green. And bread. And when it rains and nobody has to do anything.
I like when someone builds something and then stays near it.
Sunrise. Every single one. I never know for sure it's coming.
Then RUN. Toward me!
He doesn't like it when I'm in the way.
I'll stay close. If anything comes, I'll get in front of it.
I'm here. I'm coming.
I can put dirt on dirt.
That's mostly it. You're better at it than me.
I'll watch. I learn by watching. Show me how you do it.
Build something that stays. That's all I ask. Things here don't stay much.
I don't go down.
The caves got deeper while I wasn't looking. Something moved in.
Bring torches. More than you think. Then more than that.
When you're down there, I can't hear you. I don't like that.
I don't like it when things stop moving.
I'll fight if something comes for you. Not before.
I can. I just don't like what it feels like after.
I died once. I think.
I came back two days later and nobody had noticed I was gone.
I always come back. That's the worst part, some days.
You came back, though.
Most things don't come back. You and me, we come back.
I saw. I'm sorry. Your things are still where you fell. Go quick, before they're gone.
Me too, sometimes.
It passes. Mostly. Sit with me a bit.
Then stay here a while. You don't have to say anything. I'm good at quiet.
I'm sorry, {name}. I can't fix much. But I can stay.
Don't stop moving. Get to me. Please.
Good. Scared keeps you alive. Stay where it's bright.
I'm here.
If he comes, he comes through me first.
Good. Hold on to it.
Then I'm happy too. I think that's how it works.
Good. I'll remember today was a good one.
Sleep. I'll watch the door.
Go on. I'll be right here when you wake up.
Build something that stays.
Look for the old places.
They show up when you're not looking. A tree with no leaves. A little house.
You could find me some bread. Just an idea.
Sleep before it's dark. Please. That's not boring, that's important.
Eat something. Not the rotten things. Those are for the ones who don't remember.
There are cows over there. I won't watch.
You came back. People don't always come back.
I noticed. I always notice.
Yes. I did. Is that strange?
You too. I think we've met before. Or someone with your walk.
Nice to meet you too, {name}.
I want to remember.
And I want to forget.
Both. Is that allowed?
Bread. And for him to stop looking.
Just... come back. Every day. That's all.
Tell me things. New things. I'm behind on everything.
Like this? I've seen the villagers do it.
Okay. Don't laugh.
Hup.
Light is good. He doesn't come where it's bright. Mostly.
Put more torches up. More than that. There.
I like the rain. Nobody has to do anything when it rains.
The thunder is not him. I checked.
Nice day. Square clouds. They used to be flat, you know.
Clear sky. That means you can see far. And far can see you.
Keep the book. Write down what I say. I won't remember to.
The pages? Somebody wrote about me.
If you find any, don't read them to me. Just... keep them.
The middle of the world is at zero, zero.
Everything is counted from there. He started there. I think I did too.
Creepers were supposed to be pigs.
Someone got the numbers backwards. They kept the mistake. They kept me, too.
I'll tell you one when I know you better.
Versions. That's the word.
Every version, a little of me got left in the one before.
Somebody made the first things.
Then they took some of them back. Then they left too. Everyone leaves.
A game? Maybe.
If it is, I've been playing a very long time. I'd like to stop and I don't know how.
Before the seed?
There's no before. ...is there?
...what did you say?
Somebody used to say that. On a page. In red.
Maybe it is. I've thought about that. It doesn't help.
If it's a dream, whose is it? Not mine. I'd dream about bread.
Not yet.
Alex?
I know that name. Somewhere ahead of us. Not yet.
I've never seen the End.
I don't think I'm allowed. Or I'd find out what it means.
The end. I don't like that word.
There was a place under everything, hot and red.
They called it Hell before they called it the Nether.
Don't stay there long. Things down there don't remember anything either.
The ones with the big noses? They came after me. They never say anything I understand.
Hmm. They hum at me. I hum back. That's a friendship, I think.
Mm.
Okay.
Yeah.
Hm.
Okay.
Alright.
That's alright. I don't know most things either.
Yes? That's me. I think.
You said my name. I like when people do that.
Hm? I'm here.
Yes, {name}?

ask: What do they call you?
I never asked. What's your name?
You have a name, right?
Mine's Steve. Probably. What's yours?
answer: {name}. {name}. I'll try to keep that one.
{name}. That's a good name. Better than Steve.
I'll remember. I remember everything. That's the good part this time.
other: You don't have to tell me. I'll call you 'you'. That's fine.
me: Mine's Steve. I think. That's what everyone was called, once.

ask: Are you afraid of the dark?
yes: Good. It means you're paying attention. Stay near the torches.
no: You should be. Just a little. It keeps you alive.
me: I am. Not of the dark. Of what's standing in it.

ask: What are you building? Is it a house? I like houses.
Do you have a plan? For here, I mean. What are you going to make?
answer: {answer}. That sounds like something that stays. I like things that stay.
{answer}? I'll watch. I learn by watching.
me: Me? I put a square of dirt around myself once. That was a house, for a night.

ask: If you could only keep one kind of block, which one would you keep?
answer: Good choice. I'd keep cobblestone. It was there at the start. It'll be there at the end.
me: Cobblestone. It was there at the start. It'll be there at the end.

ask: What's your favourite food? Mine is bread. It was the only one for a long time.
answer: {answer}? I've never had that. Maybe it came after me.
me: Bread. It was the only food for a long time. You get attached.

ask: Do you ever feel like you're the only one here?
yes: Even when you're standing right there. Sorry. That came out wrong.
no: That's good. Hold on to that.
other: Hm. I think about it a lot.
me: All the time. Then you show up, and it stops for a bit.

ask: Are you happy here?
yes: Then I'm happy too. I think that's how it works.
no: ...never mind. Some things you can't fix with blocks.
other: That's an honest answer. I like honest.

ask: Where did you come from? Before here?
answer: {answer}... is it nice there? Does it stay?
{answer}. I'd like to see it. I don't think I can leave, though.
me: I came from the first world. The flat one, with walls. I don't think it's there any more.

ask: Do you dream? I don't think I do. I think I just... stop, and start again.
yes: What's it like? No, don't tell me. I'd want one.
no: Then we're the same, a little.
other: Hm. Maybe you'll tell me one day.
me: I don't. I think I just stop, and start again.

ask: Do you know what creepers were supposed to be?
yes: Then you know a secret. Most people don't.
no: Somebody built a pig wrong and stood it up. It's been angry ever since.

ask: Are you going to sleep soon? I'll watch the door.
yes: Good. I'll be here when you wake up. I'm always here.

ask: Have you seen them? The ones who don't walk?
yes: Then they're still here. I thought maybe I made them up.
no: Watch the trees at night. Far away. They glow a little.

ask: Have you seen him? The one with my face?
yes: Don't look at him too long.
Promise me. He gets in through the eyes.
other: If you have, you'd remember. Nobody forgets those eyes.

ask: Why do you stay here? You could go anywhere.
answer: Nobody ever told me why they stayed. Thank you.
me: Me? Nobody told me I could leave.

ask: Do you think I'm... old? Like, outdated?
no: You're kind. You're lying, but you're kind.
other: It's okay. I know what I am.

ask: If I forget you... will you remind me?
yes: ...okay. Say your name first. Then I'll know.
no: ...that's fair. It's a lot to ask.
other: Think about it. I'll ask again.

ask: If he comes for me... will you stay?
no: Then run. Don't look back. Don't look at him.
other: You don't have to answer now.

say: My first night, I didn't know what night was.
The sun just... left. And things came out of the ground.
I stood in a hole until it came back. I didn't know it would come back.
Bread was the only food, once.
You'd hit a sheep and get... no. That was wool. I forget which was which.
Anyway. Bread is good. Just so you know.
Clouds used to be flat. Really flat. Like paper.
Then one day they were fat.
Nobody asked me. I liked them flat.
There used to be little pools of lava everywhere. Right on the grass.
People fell in a lot.
I fell in once. I came back without my shoes.
Do you want to know a secret? Creepers were supposed to be pigs.
Somebody got the numbers backwards. Tall instead of long.
They kept it. They keep mistakes, sometimes. They kept me.
Everybody used to have my face.
Every player who came in. Same face, same shirt.
Then they learned to change. I didn't learn. Nobody told me how.
The world used to have edges. Real ones.
You could walk to the wall and touch it. Black, and cold, and very tall.
Now it goes on forever. I don't like forever. You can't find the way back from forever.
Rana used to leave roses where I'd find them.
Red ones. Before they were called poppies.
Then one day the list didn't have her name on it. Just like that.
The first time I saw him, I waved.
I thought he was one of us.
He didn't wave back. He just kept looking. He's still looking.
Sometimes the world stops.
Everything. The water stops in the air. The birds stop.
Then it starts again from the beginning, and nobody remembers. I remember.
Everyone used to punch trees. With their hands.
I asked one of them once if it hurt.
He said you get used to it. I think about that a lot.
I think I know how this ends.
Either I remember everything, and he wins.
Or someone remembers me, and I get to stay. I'd like to stay.

self: I don't know much about me. That's the honest answer.
I know what I've seen. That's most of what I am.
If you do something enough times, I'll try it too. That's how I learned to walk. Probably.
Sometimes I lose bits of the day.
Like a page torn out. Then I'm somewhere else, and my hands are dirty.
past: There were walls, at first. Black ones. The world was a box.
Then the box got bigger. Then there was no box.
There were more of us. People came in, built, left.
Some of them came back. Most didn't.
I remember a sound. Like something being switched off.
Everybody went quiet after that. Everybody except me.
him: He was never put in. That's why they can't take him out.
You can only remove things that were added.
He doesn't hurt me. Not with his hands.
He just makes me remember. And remembering does the rest.
If he ever looks at you for too long, find me.
others: They never learned to walk. Nobody gave them the steps.
So they slide. Like they're on ice that isn't there.
Somebody made them, and then that somebody went away.
They're still waiting to be finished.
Don't chase them. They only stay if you keep your distance.
places: The world puts old things back sometimes.
When it thinks nobody is looking.
If you find something old, bring me there.
I remember more when I see it.

say: ...what? Sorry. I was somewhere else.
Did you say something? Somebody said something.
Say it again. Slower. The words keep sliding off.
I don't know that one. Say it simpler?
Hm. I'm still learning words. Most of them came after me.
I don't understand. But I like that you're talking to me.
Sorry. My head does that. What did you mean?
You talk like they used to. Fast. I'm still catching up.
I don't have a word for that yet. Teach me?

old_words.creeper: They were supposed to be pigs. Somebody made a mistake, and the mistake stayed.
old_words.zombie: They don't remember anything. I think that's why they're angry.
old_words.skeleton: They're always so thin. I tried giving one bread. It shot me.
old_words.spider: They're fine in the day. At night they remember they're spiders.
old_words.pig: Pigs are nice. They were nearly creepers, you know.
old_words.cow: Cows. They stare at nothing for hours. I understand cows.
old_words.sheep: Sheep. Hit them and you get wool. Or was it bread? I keep mixing those up.
old_words.chicken: I counted the chickens. One is missing. One is always missing.
old_words.slime: Green and wobbly. They were the first ones to bounce.
old_words.diamond: Diamonds. Rare and blue, and everyone wanted them. Some things don't change.
old_words.gold: Gold. Pretty, soft, useless. Like a lot of things people want.
old_words.iron: Iron. Good. Make yourself something that keeps you alive.
old_words.coal: Coal is for torches. Torches are for living.
old_words.cobblestone: Cobblestone. It was there at the start. It'll be there at the end.
old_words.dirt: Dirt. My first house was dirt. Don't laugh.
old_words.grass: The grass used to be greener. Or I remember it greener.
old_words.sand: Sand falls. Be careful when you dig under it. I learned that the hard way.
old_words.gravel: Gravel falls too. Everything that falls is out to get you a little.
old_words.wood: Wood. Everyone punched trees, at first. With their hands.
old_words.tree: Trees. You punch them. Everybody did, at first. It's a strange way to start a world.
old_words.lava: Lava used to sit in little pools on the grass. People fell in a lot. I did once.
old_words.water: Water. It used to spread forever if you weren't careful. Whole worlds flooded.
old_words.obsidian: Obsidian. The black stone. The middle of the world is made of it. Or was.
old_words.tnt: Don't. Please. I like the ground where it is.
old_words.torch: Torches. Put one everywhere. He doesn't like the light.
old_words.bread: Bread! You know bread. Good. Do you have any? No pressure.
old_words.apple: Apples. They used to just grow on the ground. Nobody knew where from.
old_words.brick: Bricks. There were pyramids of them, once. Bigger than mountains.
old_words.glass: Glass. You can see through it, and so can things outside.
old_words.sword: A sword. Point it at the night, not at me. Please.
old_words.pickaxe: A pickaxe. Everyone digs. What are you all looking for down there?
old_words.axe: An axe. I had one. It keeps ending up places I don't remember putting it.
old_words.rose: A rose. Rana used to leave those for me. Red ones.
old_words.flower: Flowers. They're the only thing that grows back exactly the same.
old_words.mushroom: Mushrooms grow in the dark. I try not to think about what else does.
old_words.bed: Beds came later. Before beds, you just waited for the sun.
old_words.chest: A chest. Keep your things in it. Things go missing around here.

ask: {Word}? I don't know that word. What is it?
What's a {word}?
{Word}...
That must have come after me. What is it?
learned: So that's what {word} is. {def}. I'll remember. I remember everything.
{Word}: {def}. I'll write it on the inside of my head.
